basis: TechCrunch (2013-02-18): Quad Learning 'has raised more than $11 million in seed and series A financing from New Atlantic Ventures, Swan and Legend Fund, NEA, Comcast Ventures and others'; the Washington Business Journal headline of the same week names New Enterprise Associates and Comcast Ventures as the launch investors. A round naming NEA, so fund money (D2).

note: Washington, D.C. community-college honors and transfer programmes (TechCrunch). NEA came in with the $11M seed and Series A announced together in February 2013, and no source says which half NEA bought, so the stage is undetermined (were it the seed, the April 2014 Series B would graduate it). Status: Inside Higher Ed (2019-05-22) reports American Honors was sold to Wellspring International Education in 2018 in a distress sale worth a small fraction of what Quad raised; Wikipedia dates the sale November 2018.

basis: Hypebot (2021-11-23): Royal's $55M Series A 'was led by Andreessen Horowitz's a16z Crypto fund with participation from ... CAA, NEA's Connect Ventures, ... Founders Fund and Paradigm'. Connect Ventures is IN under decisions.md's Connect Ventures re-derivation (T1): NEA's own Form ADV lists Connect Ventures I, L.P. among the private funds its adviser advises.

note: Music-rights marketplace founded in 2021 by 3LAU and JD Ross, headquartered in Austin (Wikipedia). Connect Ventures entered at the November 2021 Series A; CoinDesk's account of the August 2021 $16M seed lists Paradigm, Founders Fund, Atomic and angels, not Connect. Status private, disagreeing with the a16z row's defunct (its status came from a Wikidata join to a Swedish namesake): the song-drop marketplace was sunset in 2024, but royal.io still presents a live product, 'Programmable Money for Creators' (read 2026-09-30). Momentum check 2026-09-30 (Google News, the company's name with round and exit words): no round after the Series A, which disclosed no valuation.

basis: Scalix's own About page (captured 2003-06-21, quoted in the recall triage): 'Scalix is backed by leading Silicon Valley venture firms Mayfield and New Enterprise Associates'; Wikipedia: 'The company was funded by venture firms New Enterprise Associates (NEA), Mohr Davidow Ventures (MDV) and Mayfield Fund.' Named as a funding firm by the company itself (D2). Not on NEA's own list in any era.

note: Linux email and groupware server built on HP's OpenMail code, founded in 2002 by Julie Hanna at Mayfield, San Mateo. Stage from the model: Crunchbase's transcription (a vendor, listed not cited) has a $13.2M Series A in June 2003 with Mayfield and NEA, which matches the company's own June 2003 page naming exactly those two backers; Mohr Davidow came in later. Xandros bought Scalix in July 2007 (Wikipedia), and resold it to Sebring Software in 2011.

basis: The company's release (2026-06-03): 'The Series A of $20 million was co-led by Keith Rabois at Khosla Ventures and Nicole Quinn at Connect Ventures'; Pulse 2.0 (2026-06-02) also names New Enterprise Associates among the participants. Connect Ventures is IN under decisions.md's Connect Ventures re-derivation (T1): NEA's own Form ADV lists Connect Ventures I, L.P. among the private funds its adviser advises.

note: Social platform for AI-built mini apps. Connect Ventures co-led the $20M Series A of June 2026; the release names the seed's lead (Mayfield) and its returning investors (a16z speedrun, A*, MVP) and not Connect, so the Series A is the entry. City aligned with the a16z row (Sunnyvale, web verified); the release carries a San Francisco dateline. Momentum check 2026-09-30 (Google News, valuation and billion words): no $1B+ priced round; the Series A disclosed no valuation.

basis: GamesBeat (2022-02-01): 'Epic is investing in Spire alongside existing investor Connect Ventures, an investment partnership formed by Creative Artists Agency (CAA) and New Enterprise Associates (NEA)'; Deadline's headline of 2020-06-24 has CAA and NEA forming Connect Ventures and backing Spire, Connect's first investment. Connect Ventures is IN under decisions.md's Connect Ventures re-derivation (T1): NEA's own Form ADV lists Connect Ventures I, L.P. among the private funds its adviser advises.

note: Los Angeles animation studio making features with real-time game-engine tools (GamesBeat). Connect Ventures backed it at formation in June 2020; no source names that round, and GamesBeat does not name the $20M 2022 round either, so the stage is undetermined. Still operating: Asia Asset Management reported a Temasek investment in March 2026.

basis: SportsPro (2024-06): Connect Ventures, 'an investment partnership between Creative Artists Agency (CAA) and venture capital firm New Enterprise Associates (NEA)', co-led TMRW's Series A with Dynasty Equity and 'also co-led the initial fundraising round for TMRW' (The Hollywood Reporter, 2022-11-02: 'TMRW Sports Scores Investments From CAA's Connect Ventures'). Connect Ventures is IN under decisions.md's Connect Ventures re-derivation (T1): NEA's own Form ADV lists Connect Ventures I, L.P. among the private funds its adviser advises.

note: Sports company of Tiger Woods, Rory McIlroy and Mike McCarley that runs the TGL golf league (founded 2022). Connect co-led the initial round of November 2022, which no source names, so the stage is undetermined. The June 2024 Series A valued TMRW at about $500M (SportsPro); September 2026 reports (Front Office Sports via Dallas Sports Journal) have a new round near $1B still in talks, not a priced event. City from company-profile listings (Winter Park, Florida), inferred, not cited.

basis: Wikipedia: the $45M round of 2015-10-27 was 'led by GreatPoint Ventures and existing investors including New Enterprise Associates and Caterpillar' (citing the New York Times); Business Insider via Yahoo Finance (2017-02-01): 'Uptake Technologies' other investments include ... Lightbank, New Enterprise Associates'. A round naming NEA, so fund money (D2). Not on NEA's own list in any era.

note: Chicago industrial AI and predictive-maintenance company (founded 2014). Mark re-pinned to the $117M Series D led by Baillie Gifford at $2.3B (AgFunderNews, 2017-12-01), stale; no newer priced round. Bosch agreed to buy Uptake on 2026-03-19 (Bosch release, terms not disclosed, 'upon closing' language) and no closing was found by 2026-09-30, so the row stays private. Stage undetermined: Wikipedia calls NEA an existing investor at the October 2015 round, which puts NEA's entry at an earlier 2015 round no source names, while a vendor dates NEA's first check to that October round itself; the two readings differ (Series A or Growth).

basis: NEA's own Schedule 13D on Pharmos (2006): 'NEA 10 acquired 1,880,824 shares of Common Stock ... on October 25, 2006 in exchange for 7,500,075 shares of Series D Convertible Preferred Stock ... of Vela Pharmaceuticals, Inc.' and notes convertible into Series D. An NEA fund held Vela privately before Pharmos bought it; Pharmos' 2006 proxy names New Enterprise Associates among Vela's three principal shareholders. The Pharmos stock is the sale consideration (D8), so the base row pharmos is the acquirer and Vela the member.

note: Brain-gut drug developer in Ewing, New Jersey (Pharmos proxy, 2006). Vela sold Series A and B in 1999-2000, Series C, and in 2002 a Series D ($24.8M of proceeds); at the end of 2005 7,500,075 Series D shares were outstanding, exactly the number NEA 10 exchanged in the merger, and NEA's 13D names no other series, so NEA entered at the Series D (Growth). Pharmos completed the purchase on 2006-10-25.

basis: TechCrunch (2007-12-18): Vuze, 'previously known as Azureus, has raised $20M in a Series C round of funding led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA)', with Redpoint, Greycroft, BV Capital and Jarl Mohn as existing investors. A round NEA led, so fund money (D2).

note: Vuze, Inc. (formerly Azureus), the BitTorrent client and video platform. NEA was new at the $20M Series C it led in December 2007 (TechCrunch lists the earlier A and B without NEA), so the entry is Growth. Status and city aligned with the Headline and Redpoint rows (defunct, Palo Alto); Wikipedia's Vuze article says Spigot acquired Vuze in December 2010 without a source, and its Vuze, Inc. article places the company in San Mateo.

Food-ingredient maker in Bedford, Massachusetts (its 8-K address). Stake Technology Ltd. (later SunOpta) bought Opta through a $2.50-a-share tender offer: its subsidiary accepted about 10.1M tendered shares on 2002-12-04 (Opta 8-K of 2002-12-09), and Opta deregistered that month.

Dermatology drug company in Foster City, California. Mylan Laboratories acquired Penederm by merger, 0.68 Mylan share per Penederm share, approved at the special meeting of 1998-10-02 (definitive proxy of 1998-09-01); Penederm filed its Form 15 the same day.

Platinum Software of Irvine, renamed Epicor Software in 1999 after buying DataWorks. Apax Partners bought Epicor through a tender offer in April and May 2011 (Epicor deregistered on 2011-05-26). Aligned with the IVP row (acquired, Irvine).

Dental and ophthalmic laser maker in Irvine, California. It suspended operations in March 2000, filed Chapter 11, retained an adviser to liquidate all assets and sold the pieces separately (Topomax IP to LaserSight, its Ophthalmic Imaging Systems stake to MediVision, the ophthalmic laser division to SurgiLight); its Joint Plan of Liquidation took effect on 2001-10-09 (8-K). No buyer took the business as a whole, so defunct. The later filings come from the estate representative's office in Aliso Viejo.

Genomics drug-discovery company at North Torrey Pines Road, La Jolla (San Diego). It agreed on 1997-11-02 to merge with a subsidiary of Arris Pharmaceutical (8-K of 1997-11-12); its Form 15 of 1998-01-09 reports a single holder of record, and the combined company took the name Axys Pharmaceuticals.

Summit Medical Systems of Minneapolis, renamed Celeris Corporation in 1999 and later based in Nashville as a clinical research organisation. Shareholders were asked on 2002-06-26 to approve the sale of substantially all of Celeris' assets to Statprobe, Inc. and a plan of liquidation (definitive proxy of 2002-05-31); the record date for the dissolution payments followed in November 2002 and the company deregistered in December. The business continued under Statprobe, so acquired; city is the last known.

Versicor, an anti-infective drug developer in Fremont, California, combined with Biosearch Italia in 2003 and took the name Vicuron Pharmaceuticals, based in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania (last known). Pfizer bought Vicuron for $29.10 a share in cash (merger proxy of 2005-07-19); Vicuron deregistered on 2005-09-14.
